Initial Vaccinations Our puppy’s first jabs (often for Distemper, Parvovirus, Leptospirosis, Hepatitis) were at around 6-8 weeks old.

Boosters Annual booster vaccinations are crucial to maintain your Staffy’s immunity throughout their life.

01 Appetite Changes in Puppy Appetite or Thirst: A sudden decrease or increase in food or water intake can be a sign of illness.
02 Lethargy Lethargy or Unusual Tiredness: If your normally energetic Staffy puppy is unusually quiet, listless, or sleeping excessively.
03 Vomiting Vomiting or Diarrhoea: Occasional upset stomachs can happen, but persistent or severe vomiting/diarrhoea, especially with blood, warrants immediate attention.
04 Limping Puppy Limping or Difficulty Moving: Any signs of pain or struggle with movement could indicate a joint issue or injury.
05 Itching Excessive itching, licking, or skin redness can be concerning for any owner, especially if you notice your puppy itchy skin or puppy scratching ear frequently.
06 Coughing Puppy coughing, sneezing, or nasal discharge are symptoms to watch out for, as persistent respiratory signs might indicate a cold or, more seriously, kennel cough in puppies .
